title: Restricted Sight Distance Criteria for Protected Left-Turn Phasing
summary: Figure 2 on sheet 3 of 7 of S-497.0 shows restricted sight distance caused by vertical alignment (a crest). A left-turn motorist with a 3.5 ft eye height and an opposing through vehicle 4.25 ft high cannot see each other over the crest. The required sight distance is the (5.0 + 0.5n) second value from Table A, and protected left-turn phasing is required if any minimum sight distance is not met.
description: Figure 2 (sheet 3 of 7), side elevation: A profile view of a roadway crest drawn as a single curved line, with a car at each end sloping down away from the crest. At the left is the left-turn motorist, labeled "Left-turn motorist" with "Height of eye-3.5 feet". At the right is the opposing vehicle, labeled "Thru motorist" with "Height of vehicle-4.25 feet". A dashed horizontal line runs from the top of the left car, and another from the top of the right car, toward the crest, showing that the line of sight is blocked by the rise of the road between them. A short vertical tick with an arrowed leader sits above each car and points to a single callout between them reading "See Table A for (5.0 + 0.5n) sec, where n = number of opposing thru lanes", meaning the required sight distance for each driver is taken from Table A for that time gap. Below the drawing is the statement "Protected left turn phasing is required if any minimum sight distance is not met and left turns are allowed." The figure caption reads "Example of Restricted Sight Distance Due To Vertical Alighment" (spelled as drawn) and "Figure 2". The title block gives City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Restricted Sight Distance Criteria for Protected Left-Turn Phasing, Drawing No. S-497.0, sheet 3 of 7.
notes:
1. See Table A for (5.0 + 0.5n) seconds (sec), where n = number of opposing through (thru) lanes.
2. Protected left turn phasing is required if any minimum sight distance is not met and left turns are allowed.
Figure labels: Left-turn motorist, height of eye 3.5 feet. Thru motorist, height of vehicle 4.25 feet.
Figure caption: Example of Restricted Sight Distance Due To Vertical Alighment (as drawn). Figure 2.

title: Restricted Sight Distance Criteria for Protected Left-Turn Phasing
summary: Figure 3 on sheet 4 of 7 of S-497.0 shows restricted sight distance at a signalized intersection where a landscaped median on a horizontal curve blocks the view of opposing traffic. Sight distances are measured along Line A and checked against Table A values of 5.5 sec and 6.0 sec. Protected left-turn phasing is required if any minimum distance along Line A is not met, and Line B should be examined per Figure 6 if the obstruction is short.
description: Figure 3 (sheet 4 of 7), plan view: An intersection plan with the arterial curving through the top half of the sheet and a cross street running left and right across the middle. The arterial's raised median is hatched and planted with tree symbols, and it follows the curve, so the trees and curb block the view along the inside of the curve. Dashed lane lines show the opposing travel lanes on both sides of the median. Opposing cars are drawn in the lanes on the curve: two near the top of the curve and two lower, close to the intersection. In the intersection, at the bottom, a left-turn car waits in the intersection with two dashed sight lines fanning from it toward the opposing approach, labeled Line A (left line) and Line B (right line). At the left, two dimension leaders with arrowheads run from the opposing cars back to a horizontal extension line through the left-turn car position. The first, farther dimension is labeled "See Table A for 6.0 sec" and the nearer one "See Table A for 5.5 sec", showing the required sight distances measured back from the left-turn car's location. Text on the right side of the sheet reads "Protected left turn phasing is required if any minimum sight distance along Line A is not met and left turns are allowed. See Figure 6 and examine Line B distances if the obstruction distance is relatively short." Caption: "Example of Restricted Sight Distance Due To Physical Obstruction", Figure 3. Title block: Drawing No. S-497.0, sheet 4 of 7.
notes:
1. See Table A for 6.0 sec.
2. See Table A for 5.5 sec.
3. Protected left turn phasing is required if any minimum sight distance along Line A is not met and left turns are allowed. See Figure 6 and examine Line B distances if the obstruction distance is relatively short.
Figure labels: Line A, Line B.
Figure caption: Example of Restricted Sight Distance Due To Physical Obstruction. Figure 3.

title: Restricted Sight Distance Criteria for Protected Left-Turn Phasing
summary: Figure 4 on sheet 5 of 7 of S-497.0 shows infrequently restricted sight distance where a negatively offset left-turn lane has light opposing left-turn demand. It applies to arterials with a cross street under 10,000 ADT and generally fewer than 2 opposing left-turning vehicles per cycle, where queues are short and usually clear. A left turn study may be used instead, in which case Figure 5 applies.
description: Figure 4 (sheet 5 of 7), plan view: A four-leg signalized intersection with the arterial running vertically and a cross street running horizontally. The arterial has a hatched raised median. In the upper approach the median narrows toward the intersection with a curved, jogged edge, forming a negatively offset left-turn lane on its left side, marked with a dimension X between the dashed lane line and the offset edge of the median. A white left-turn arrow is drawn beside the median and a single car is shown queued in the left-turn lane next to the stop line. A leader on the queued car's lane reads "Generally < 2 vehicles per cycle". The lower approach has a hatched median, a left-turn lane with a white left-turn arrow, and lane lines. Two cars with dashed curved paths cross the intersection box, showing opposing left turns. The cross street to the right is labeled "Generally less than 10,000 ADT". A paragraph at the right reads: "This figure is for general use on arterial highways with negatively offset left turn lanes at intersections with lower volume cross streets and /or low volume left turns from the arterial streets. In these situations the queuing from the opposing left turns will be short or infrequent and will usually clear during the cycle, thus resulting in a period of unrestricted sight distance for permissive left turns." A second paragraph states the infrequently restricted assumption and the option of a left turn study. Caption: "Example of Infrequently Restricted Sight Distance Due to Negatively Offset Left Turn Lanes with Light Opposing Left Turn Demand", Figure 4. Title block: Drawing No. S-497.0, sheet 5 of 7.
notes:
1. Generally less than (<) 2 vehicles per cycle (figure label at the queued left-turn car).
2. Cross street: generally less than 10,000 average daily traffic (ADT) (figure label).
3. This figure is for general use on arterial highways with negatively offset left turn lanes at intersections with lower volume cross streets and/or low volume left turns from the arterial streets. In these situations the queuing from the opposing left turns will be short or infrequent and will usually clear during the cycle, thus resulting in a period of unrestricted sight distance for permissive left turns.
4. Infrequently restricted sight distance generally would be assumed to occur if the cross street has less than 10,000 ADT and opposing left turns are less than two cars per cycle during the peak hour. However, a left turn study may be conducted in place of these guidelines to document the frequency of restricted sight distance. When such a study is conducted, refer to Figure 5.
Figure caption: Example of Infrequently Restricted Sight Distance Due to Negatively Offset Left Turn Lanes with Light Opposing Left Turn Demand. Figure 4.

title: Restricted Sight Distance Criteria for Protected Left-Turn Phasing
summary: Figure 5 on sheet 6 of 7 of S-497.0 shows frequently restricted sight distance at a negatively offset left-turn lane with moderate opposing left-turn demand, typically on an arterial or high-volume collector cross street over 10,000 ADT. It plots Table A sight distances of 6.0 sec and 5.5 sec against a queue of opposing left-turners and gives a table of the negative offset X for lane widths W of 9 to 12 ft. If sight distance is frequently restricted and below Table A, first remove the island and restripe, otherwise protected phasing is required.
description:
Figure 5 (sheet 6 of 7), plan view: A four-leg signalized intersection with the arterial vertical and a hatched raised median. On the upper approach the median is jogged to create a negatively offset opposing left-turn lane. Two dimension lines at the left, drawn back from the intersection along the arterial, are labeled "See Table A for 6.0 sec" (longer) and "See Table A for 5.5 sec" (shorter), with extension lines to the opposing cars. A dashed sight line runs diagonally from the left-turn driver past the queued opposing left-turn vehicles toward a distant approaching car. Width W is dimensioned twice, at the left-turn lane and at the queue position, and offset X is dimensioned at the lane line near the far opposing car and near the left-turn position. Two cars are stacked in the opposing left-turn lane near the stop line. Inside the intersection box, the left-turning car is drawn in two positions with dimensions: 5' near the opposing queue car, 2' on the near side, X at the lane line, 10' between the two turning vehicles along the diagonal, 8' across the turning vehicle, 2' and 6' at the lower car. A curved dashed turning path is labeled "Turning path for 10' separation". The lower approach shows a hatched median, a left-turn lane with a left-turn arrow, and lane lines. The cross street on the right is labeled "Generally, an Arterial or High Volume Collector Street (10,000 ADT)".

Table (W versus X), W, ft / X, ft: 9 / 1.5; 10 / 2.0; 11 / 2.5; 12 / 3.0.

Three paragraphs of text sit to the right of the plan and are transcribed in the notes. Caption: "Example of Frequently Restricted Sight Distance Due To Negatively Offset Left Turn Lanes with Moderate Opposing Left Turn Demand", Figure 5. Title block: Drawing No. S-497.0, sheet 6 of 7.
notes:
1. See Table A for 6.0 sec.
2. See Table A for 5.5 sec.
3. Turning path for 10' separation.
4. Generally, an Arterial or High Volume Collector Street (10,000 ADT).
5. Table: W, ft / X, ft. 9 / 1.5. 10 / 2.0. 11 / 2.5. 12 / 3.0.
6. This figure is for general use on arterial highways or high volume collector streets with negatively offset left turn lanes at higher volume cross streets. In these situations, the negative offset, in combination with moderate opposing left turn demand, may result in frequently restricted sight distance for permissive left turns.
7. The determination of frequently restricted sight distance can be determined by: 1) assessing the frequency of restricted sight distance, and 2) measuring the sight distance. Restricted sight distance will be assumed to occur frequently with moderate opposing left-turn demand if the cross street has more than 10,000 ADT. However, a left turn study may be conducted in place of this guideline to document the actual frequency of restricted sight distance. If the study shows that more than 15% of queues do not clear during their cycles of arrival during the peak hour then restricted visibility is judged to be frequent.
8. The sight distance can be plotted on a striping plan as shown in this figure or as measured in the field. If the sight distance is frequently restricted and is less than the values shown in Table A then remedial action should be taken.
9. Remedial action should first consider removal of the raised median island and restriping to eliminate the negative offset. If this is not feasible then protected left turn phasing is required.
Figure caption: Example of Frequently Restricted Sight Distance Due To Negatively Offset Left Turn Lanes with Moderate Opposing Left Turn Demand. Figure 5.

title: Restricted Sight Distance Criteria for Protected Left-Turn Phasing
summary: Figure 6 on sheet 7 of 7 of S-497.0 shows frequently restricted sight distance where moderate opposing left-turn demand combines with a right horizontal curve. Left-turn drivers see downstream of Line A (first queued vehicle) and upstream of Line B (end of the 85th percentile queue) but not between. If the Table A distances of 5.5 sec and 6.0 sec fall between the lines, protected phasing is required. Without observations the 85th percentile queue is assumed to be 40 V/N feet.
description:
Figure 6 (sheet 7 of 7), plan view: A four-leg signalized intersection where the arterial approaches from the top along a curve to the right, with a raised median and an opposing left-turn lane that is negatively offset. The upper approach shows a queue of about six opposing left-turn cars lined up in the left-turn lane beside the median, then a gap, then further opposing through cars farther up the curve. Offset X and lane width W dimensions are marked repeatedly along the curve, at the queue and at the far cars. Two dashed sight lines are drawn from the waiting left-turn driver: LINE A passes to the left of the first queued vehicle and LINE B passes beside the last vehicle in the queue, with the queue length between them. Dimension leaders along the curve are labeled "6.0 sec. maximum - See Table A" and "5.5 sec. maximum - See Table A" (the distances beyond Line B, drawn farther out along the curve) and "See Table A for 6.0 sec." and "See Table A for 5.5 sec." (the distances measured from Line A). Vertical extension lines at the left of the intersection tie these four dimensions to the stop-bar position. Inside the intersection box, the opposing left-turn car and the left-turn car at the bottom are dimensioned: 5' (opposing car, near edge), 1' (offset to the dashed sight line), 10' (separation between the two turning vehicles along the line of sight), 8' (turning vehicle width), 1' and 3' at the lower car. Curved dashed turning paths are labeled "Turning path for 10' separation". The lower approach has a left-turn lane with a white left-turn arrow and lane lines. A cross street runs left to right.

Table (W versus X), W, ft / X, ft: 9 / 1.5; 10 / 2.0; 11 / 2.5; 12 / 3.0. The table sits to the left of the plan view.

Text block at the upper left, transcribed in the notes. Caption: "Example of Frequently Restricted Sight Distance Due To Moderate Opposing Left Turn Demand in Combination with Right Horizontal Curvature", Figure 6. Title block: Drawing No. S-497.0, sheet 7 of 7.
notes:
1. Left turning motorists can see downstream of Line A (which is defined by the first vehicle in a queue) and upstream of Line B, which is defined by the last vehicle in an 85th percentile queue. They cannot, however, see between Lines A and B. If opposing vehicles can be seen at the required sight distances, shown in Table A, either downstream of Line A or upstream of Line B, then protected left turn phasing is not required. If however, the required sight distances lie between Lines A and B then visibility is inadequate for left turning decisions and protected left turn phasing is required. In the absence of documented observations, the 85th percentile queue length, in feet, is assumed to be 40 V/N, where V equals the peak hour left turn volume and N equals the number of signal cycles per hour.
2. See Table A for 6.0 sec. See Table A for 5.5 sec. 6.0 sec. maximum, see Table A. 5.5 sec. maximum, see Table A.
3. Turning path for 10' separation.
4. Table: W, ft / X, ft. 9 / 1.5. 10 / 2.0. 11 / 2.5. 12 / 3.0.
Figure labels: Line A, Line B.
Figure caption: Example of Frequently Restricted Sight Distance Due To Moderate Opposing Left Turn Demand in Combination with Right Horizontal Curvature. Figure 6.

title: Pavement Marking - PATH
summary: Shows the layout of the word PATH as a pavement marking on a grid of 2 inch by 4 inch cells, for use on bike paths. The painted area is 5.5 sq ft. The drawing was approved by the General Manager on 1-30-1998.

The grid is made of narrow vertical columns and rows, with the cell size marked at the bottom left as 2" wide (horizontal dimension) and 4" tall (vertical dimension). Conner, General Manager, drawn by M.T., Drawing No. S-498.0.
notes:

title: Guide Sign With Logo
summary: Shows sample guide signs that carry a facility name and a logo, with design notes on lettering size, colors, sheeting, logo size and placement. The minimum lettering is 8 inch upper case and 6 inch lower case for overhead signs and 6 inch upper case and 4 1/2 inch lower case for roadside signs. Roadside signs may not exceed 18 square feet, and the logo may not exceed 25% of the sign area.
description:
Sign samples: Two guide sign layouts are shown on the left side of the sheet under the heading "SIGN SAMPLES:". The upper sign is a landscape rectangle with a rounded white border. Its overall width is dimensioned D' across the top and its overall height D along the right side. A rectangle labeled "Logo" fills the upper right corner, with its width dimensioned as <= 1/2 D' (less than or equal to one half D') and its height dimensioned as <= 1/2 D. A left-pointing one-line arrow is at the upper left and the legend "Name of Facility" is centered below in two lines. The lower sign is a portrait rectangle with the same border. Its width is D' and height D, with the logo box at the upper left, again <= 1/2 D' wide and <= 1/2 D tall. A right-pointing arrow is at the upper right and "Name of Facility" in two lines is centered below.

Notes list: Eleven numbered notes are set to the right of the samples, transcribed in the notes field. The title block gives Approved January 21, 2005, John E. Fisher for Wayne K. Tanda, General Manager, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, GUIDE SIGN WITH LOGO, sheet 1 of 1, drawn by M.T., T.E. T.C., PR. T.E. T.J., Drawing No. S-499.0.
notes:
Notes:
1. Guide signs should be considered for installation as per Section 336 of the Department of Transportation's Manual of Policy and Procedures.
2. The minimum lettering size is 8" upper case and 6" lower case for overhead signs and 6" upper case and 4 1/2" lower case for roadside signs. Series E reflective white engineering grade sheeting should be used for the lettering. Total area of sign shall not exceed 18 square feet for roadside installations per Standard Plan S-476.0.
3. Signs may be fabricated by qualified private parties, with installation by LADOT field forces. Contact LADOT Coordination Section, for a list of approved sign manufacturers. However, after initial installation LADOT is responsible for maintenance and replacement of sign. If the private entity does not furnish a suitable replacement logo to LADOT when the sign need to be replaced, LADOT may elect to install a guide sign without a logo.
4. Standard Highway Series lettering and arrow style shall be used.
5. The logo size shall not exceed 25% of the sign area and shall be located in the upper left or right corner for roadside signs.
6. Sign colors should be reflectorized. Background color of sign, except for logo shall be Type 2 (Super-engineering grade) green. Legend except for logo shall be Type 3 (High Intensity) white. Logo colors shall be Type 2.
7. All lines of legend are to be centered.
8. The outside edge of the sign shall have a 3/4" reflective white border for roadside signs. There shall be a 1/2" margin between the sign edge and the border.
9. The entire sign shall be produced on 0.080 inch aluminum sheeting.
10. Sign stiffener system and hardware shall be secured to the back of the sign as required, per Standard Plan S-476.0.
11. Use one-line directional arrows as shown in S-418.5.
Sign sample labels: D' (width), D (height), logo <= 1/2 D' by <= 1/2 D, Name of Facility.

title: Supplemental Curve Warning Signing
summary: Sheet 1 of 2. Gives the method for placing supplemental curve warning signs on the outside of a curve. W1-8 chevron signs are used on long curves (arc length 100 ft or more) at approximately equal spacing S, and W1-6 signs with OM1-3 markers on short curves (arc length under 100 ft). Maximum average spacing S depends on outside curve radius R, from 25 ft at R = 100 ft up to 100 ft at R of 450 ft or more.
description:
Arc length >= 100' (W1-8 signs), plan view: A road curving to the right through a large arc, drawn as a pair of curb lines with a car at each end. R is dimensioned as the radius from the center of the curve at the lower left to the outside curb line at the top. The outside curb line carries a series of W1-8 signs, each marked "W1-8" or "W1-8's" and separated by equal spacings labeled S measured along the arc. A dashed fan of lines from the center divides the curve into thirds: the central angle Theta is shown with arcs labeled 40 degrees, and the 40 degrees is divided into three parts each labeled 40 degrees / 3. At the right, the driver's "half cone of vision" is shown with two 20 degree angles about the dashed line of sight, which is how three signs are seen at once. The caption is "Arc Length >= 100'".

Legend and formulas (upper right): S = approximate equal spacing between W1-8 signs. R = radius of outside curve. Theta = central angle of curve. L = arc length. L = 2 pi R Theta / 360. S = 2 pi R (13.3) / 360 <= 100' or table, below. Sum of S = L.

Table 1 (maximum average S by radius): R, ft / Maximum average S, ft*: 100 / 25; 150 / 35; 200 / 45; 250 / 55; 300 / 70; 350 / 80; 400 / 90; >= 450 / 100. Footnote: * See Note 6.

Arc length < 100' (W1-6 with OM1-3), plan view: A shorter, flatter curve to the right with a car at each end. Two sign locations on the outside curb are labeled "W1-6 / OM1-3". R is dimensioned from the center point at the bottom to the outside curb line, and Theta is shown as the central angle between two radial dashed lines. Labels: R = radius of outside curve, Theta = central angle of curve. The caption is "Arc Length < 100'".

Sign key (right side): W1-8 is a vertical rectangular chevron sign, W1-6 is a horizontal rectangular large arrow sign, and OM1-3 is a diamond object marker.

Title block: Approved October 4, 2005, John E. Fisher for Wayne K. Tanda, General Manager, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Supplemental Curve Warning Signing, sheet 1 of 2, drawn by M.T., Drawing No. S-501.0.
notes:
1. S = approximate equal spacing between W1-8 signs.
2. R = radius of outside curve.
3. Theta = central angle of curve.
4. L = arc length.
5. L = 2 pi R Theta / 360.
6. S = 2 pi R (13.3) / 360, not more than 100 ft, or use the table below.
7. Sum of S = L.
8. Half cone of vision: 20 degrees on each side of the line of sight. The 40 degree central angle shown is divided into three equal parts of 40 degrees / 3.
9. Maximum average S by radius*: R, ft / S, ft: 100 / 25. 150 / 35. 200 / 45. 250 / 55. 300 / 70. 350 / 80. 400 / 90. 450 or more / 100.
10. * See Note 6 (on sheet 2 of 2).
Figure labels: Arc Length >= 100'. Arc Length < 100'. W1-6 with OM1-3 on short curves. Sign key: W1-8, W1-6, OM1-3.

title: Supplemental Curve Warning Signing
summary: Sheet 2 of 2. Gives six notes for supplemental curve warning signing. It may be used on any curve and should be used where the curve design speed is at least 10 mi/hr below the speed limit. W1-6 signs with OM1-3 are used on short curves (arc length under 100 ft) and W1-8 signs on long curves (100 ft or more), spaced from the 20 degree half cone of vision as S = 2 pi R (13.3) / 360, adjusted downward to fit the arc length.
description: Notes sheet: A full-page text sheet headed "Notes" with six numbered notes and no drawing. The notes explain when supplemental curve warning signing is used, how short and long curves are defined (arc length under or at least 100 feet), how to calculate arc length L = 2 pi R Theta / 360 from the outside curb line radius R and central angle Theta, how the 13.3 degree central angle follows from a 20 degree half cone of vision with three signs seen at once (6.7 degrees between signs), and how to adjust spacing S downward. It refers to the formulas and the maximum average S table on sheet 1 of 2. The title block reads City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Supplemental Curve Warning Signing, Drawing No. S-501.0, sheet 2 of 2.
notes:
1. Supplemental curve warning signing may be used along any curve and should be used where the design speed of the curve is at least 10 miles per hour below the speed limit. Either W1-6 or W1-8 signs are used for this purpose.
2. W1-6 signs (in combination with OM1-3 signs) are used for "short" curves. One installation is posted on the outside of the curve facing each direction near the tangent of the curve. For purposes of this standard, "short" curves have arc lengths less than 100 feet.
3. W1-8 signs are used for "long" curves. Three signs must be seen in each direction at all times throughout the curve. They are installed on the outside of the curve. For purposes of this standard, "long" curves have arc lengths of 100 feet or more.
4. Determine R and Theta of the curve for the outside curb line of the street. Calculate the arc length by the formula L = 2 pi R Theta / 360, and determine if W1-6 or W1-8 signs are to be used.
5. If W 1-8 signs are to be used, the spacing is determined by the 20 degree half cone-of-vision, where three should be seen within this angle. Thus, each sign is 6.7 degrees apart, which corresponds to a 13.3 degree central angle. The maximum spacing is calculated from the formula S = 2 pi R (13.3) / 360 and rounded values are shown in the table.
6. Adjust S downward from the value derived from the formula calculation or table, where the arc length is not an integer multiple of the value. Along a given arc length S may vary somewhat due to trees, driveways or other spacing obstructions.

title: Community and Neighborhood Signs
summary: Sheet 1 of 2. Shows three LADOT sign types with dimensions: the 66 inch by 24 inch City Limit sign, the Community/District Name sign (up to 96 inches long, 18 inches tall for one line or 24 inches for two lines), and a custom Neighborhood sign limited to 36 inches by 36 inches with clipped corners. The two blue signs carry a 12 inch diameter City seal at top.
description:
City Limit Sign: A blue rectangular sign with white text and rounded corners, 66" wide by 24" tall. A 12" Dia. City of Los Angeles seal (Founded 1781) sits on the top edge near the center, partly overlapping the top of the sign. The legend is two lines, "City of" and "Los Angeles". Vertical dimensions on the left, from the top edge down: 6", 6", 2", 6", 4", totaling 24". Width 66" is dimensioned below the sign. Caption: "City Limit Sign".

Community/District Name Sign: A blue sign with white text, same style, with a 12" Dia. City seal on the top edge. The sample legend is "Atwater Village" on one line. The length is dimensioned "96" max.*" and the height on the right is dimensioned "18" one line" and "24" two lines". Vertical dimensions on the left: 6", 6", 6" (18" total). Caption: "Community/District Name Sign". An asterisk note below reads that community or district names that would exceed the 96" maximum length shall require two lines of text, with a 24" height.

Custom Neighborhood Sign: A dark green sign with light lettering, clipped (chamfered) corners, and a thin light border. The sample legend is "Castle Heights Neighborhood" in three lines, "Castle", "Heights" and "Neighborhood". Dimensioned "36" max." wide and "36" max." tall. Caption: "Custom Neighborhood Sign".

Title block: Approved 2002, Frances T. Banerjee, General Manager, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Community and Neighborhood Signs, sheet 1 of 2, drawn by M.T., Drawing No. S-502.0.
notes:
* Community or District names that would exceed the 96" maximum length shall require two lines of text, with a 24" height.
Dimension labels: City Limit Sign 66" wide by 24" tall, vertical stack 6", 6", 2", 6", 4". City seal 12" Dia. Community/District Name Sign 96" max.* long, 18" tall for one line, 24" tall for two lines, vertical stack 6", 6", 6". Custom Neighborhood Sign 36" max. by 36" max.

title: Commemorative Signs
summary: Shows a 30 inch by 30 inch commemorative street sign with brown letters on a tan background, the mission shape outline and the City Seal on top. The sample reads "Duke" Ellington Square with the description EDWARD KENNEDY ELLINGTON, BIG BAND JAZZ LEADER. Notes cover the lettering sizes for the facility name and the description, a ban on naming current elected officials, and the requirement for prior City Council or historical committee approval.
description: Sample sign: A single commemorative sign drawn in the mission shape (a square panel with rounded corners and a double outline, with a raised semicircular notch at the top center that holds the City seal). The overall size is dimensioned 30" wide across the top and 30" tall along the left side. The City of Los Angeles seal sits at the top center. Below it in serif lettering is the name "Duke" Ellington Square on two lines, and below that in all upper case smaller serif lettering EDWARD KENNEDY ELLINGTON, BIG BAND JAZZ LEADER on two lines. Five numbered notes sit below the drawing. The title block reads Approved 8/21/2000, Frances T. Banerjee, General Manager, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Commemorative Signs, sheet 1 of 1, drawn by M.T., Drawing No. S-506.0.
notes:
1. The sign shall have brown letters on a tan background with the mission shape outline and the City Seal on top.
2. The name of the intersection or facility shall use 4 inch upper case and 3 inch lower case serif letters.
3. Below the name identification shall be a short description of the person's significance, using all upper case serif letters. Refer to the Council File for guidance as to the commemorated person's significance.
4. The sign shall not include the name of any current elected official.
5. The designation shall have been approved by the City Council or an official state or federal historical committee prior to installation.
Dimension labels: 30" wide, 30" tall.

title: Pavement Marking - HUMPS
summary: Shows the layout of the word HUMPS as a pavement marking on a grid, 8'-0" wide by 8'-0" tall overall. Grid cells are 4 inches wide by 8 inches tall. The painted area is 30 sq ft and the material is alkyd thermoplastic per current LADOT specifications.
description: Layout view: The word HUMPS in five block letters, H, U, M, P and S from left to right, drawn over a grid of narrow columns and rows. The overall width is dimensioned 8'-0" below the grid and the overall height is dimensioned 8'-0" at the left. The cell size is dimensioned at the lower left as 4" wide (horizontal) and 8" tall (vertical).
